title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
label: Parlophone
tagline: The Beatles stop touring, invent a fake band to hide behind, and spend five months turning a recording studio into an instrument. Thirteen songs, one Victorian circus, and the most famous final chord in pop.
sessionsHeadline:
No more stages.
Just the studio.
sessionsText: After their last paid concert, in San Francisco in August 1966, the Beatles gave up touring. That freed them to write songs they could never play live. With producer George Martin and a 20-year-old engineer, Geoff Emerick, they spent the winter at EMI's studios on Abbey Road, bouncing four-track tapes together, varying tape speeds and cutting sound effects into the music.

tracks.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
tracks.note: Paul McCartney's idea: the Beatles pretend to be a different band, so they can escape their own image. It opens with an orchestra tuning up and an audience settling in.

tracks.title: With a Little Help from My Friends
tracks.note: Written for Ringo, introduced as the singer 'Billy Shears'. The crowd noise from the opening song runs straight into it, so the two play as one.

tracks.title: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
tracks.note: The title came from a drawing by John's four-year-old son Julian of his classmate Lucy. Lennon always denied it was a coded reference to LSD.

tracks.title: Getting Better
tracks.note: The phrase was a favourite of Jimmie Nicol, the drummer who stood in for Ringo on part of the 1964 tour. Paul's optimism is answered by John's grumpy 'it can't get no worse'.

tracks.title: Fixing a Hole
tracks.note: Recorded partly at Regent Sound in central London, because Abbey Road was booked. George Martin plays the harpsichord.

tracks.title: She's Leaving Home
tracks.note: Inspired by a newspaper story about a teenage girl who ran away from home. No Beatle plays an instrument: the strings and harp were arranged by Mike Leander.

tracks.title: Being for the Benefit of Mr. Kite!
tracks.note: John took the words almost directly from an 1843 circus poster he bought in an antique shop. For the fairground swirl, tapes of steam organ were cut into strips, shuffled and spliced back together.

tracks.title: Within You Without You
tracks.note: George Harrison's song, played with Indian musicians from London's Asian Music Circle. He is the only Beatle on it. It ends with a burst of laughter.

tracks.title: When I'm Sixty-Four
tracks.note: Paul wrote the tune as a teenager. The tape was sped up slightly to make his voice sound younger, and three clarinets give it a music-hall feel.

tracks.title: Lovely Rita
tracks.note: A love song to a traffic warden. Listen for the band blowing through combs wrapped in paper, and the heavy breathing near the end.

tracks.title: Good Morning Good Morning
tracks.note: Lennon's starting point was a cornflakes TV advert. The animal sounds at the end are ordered so each one could chase or eat the one before, and the last chicken cluck turns into the guitar of the next track.

tracks.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (Reprise)
tracks.note: Road manager Neil Aspinall suggested bringing the fake band back to close the show. Faster and rougher than the opener.

tracks.title: A Day in the Life
tracks.note: John's verses come from newspaper stories; Paul's middle section is a separate song about a morning rush. Two orchestral climbs lead to one E major chord, struck on several pianos at once and left to ring for about forty seconds.

world.what: The Six-Day War begins between Israel and its neighbours Egypt, Jordan and Syria.
The Monterey Pop Festival opens in California, launching the 'Summer of Love'. Jimi Hendrix sets his guitar on fire.
Our World, the first live global satellite broadcast, reaches hundreds of millions of viewers. Britain's contribution is the Beatles performing All You Need Is Love.
Surgeon Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant in Cape Town.

trivia: It was one of the first rock albums to print the full lyrics on the sleeve.
The cover crowd features dozens of famous faces, from Marilyn Monroe to Karl Marx. A cut-out of Gandhi was removed at EMI's request.
After A Day in the Life, the original UK vinyl has a very high-pitched tone meant for dogs, then a loop of studio chatter in the run-out groove that repeats until you lift the needle.
The BBC banned A Day in the Life from its radio stations, believing the line about wanting to 'turn you on' referred to drugs.

quiz.question: Which Beatle sings as the fictional 'Billy Shears'?
quiz.explanation: Ringo, who is introduced as Billy Shears at the end of the title track before singing With a Little Help from My Friends.

quiz.question: Where did John Lennon find the words for Being for the Benefit of Mr. Kite!?
quiz.explanation: An 1843 poster for a circus show, which he bought in an antique shop and hung in his music room.

quiz.question: Which song was the first recorded for the album?
options: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
quiz.explanation: When I'm Sixty-Four, in December 1966. Strawberry Fields Forever and Penny Lane came earlier but ended up on a single.

quiz.question: Which Beatle is the only one who plays on Within You Without You?
quiz.explanation: George Harrison, the song's writer, recorded with Indian musicians from London's Asian Music Circle.
